record.paper_title: THE LYAPIN’S NOTEBOOK: A COLLECTION OF UNSOLVED PROBLEMS IN SEMIGROUP THEORY
record.original_question: Determine all inclusive varieties whose lattices of inclusive subvarieties are finite or countable.

evidence.quote:
Problem 6.2. (G. Mashevitzky) Determine all inclusive varieties with finite or countable lattices
of inclusive subvarieties.
          A partial solution can be found in [9].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. A class of semigroups is called an inclusive variety if it can be axiomatised by a set of identical inclusions, i.e. by formulas of the form w₁ ⊆ w₂ where w₁, w₂ are semigroup words and w₁ ⊆ w₂ in a semigroup S means that for every assignment of the variables to elements of S, the value of the word w₁ is contained (as an element) in the subsemigroup generated by the value of w₂ — equivalently, every value of w₁ can be written as a value of w₂. The collection of all inclusive subvarieties of a fixed inclusive variety V, ordered by inclusion, forms a complete lattice L_in(V).

Problem. Describe (classify) all inclusive varieties V of semigroups for which the lattice L_in(V) of inclusive subvarieties is at most countable; in particular, give a characterisation of those V for which L_in(V) is finite, and of those for which L_in(V) is countably infinite.
artifact.status_search_result: A partial characterisation is known: for inclusive varieties of abelian groups, a complete description of when the lattice of inclusive subvarieties is finite has been obtained (Mashevitzky, "Nonelementary inclusive varieties of groups and semigroups", Algebra Universalis 86 (2025), no. 14). A full classification for arbitrary inclusive varieties of semigroups does not appear to be available in the literature, so the problem remains only partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Nonelementary inclusive varieties of groups and semigroups
status_evidence.snippet: An inclusive variety of abelian groups has a finite lattice of inclusive subvarieties if and only if it contains p-groups only for a finite set of primes p, it does not contain some cyclic p-group for any prime p and it does not contain some finite abelian group of exponent p for any prime p.
status_evidence.claim: Provides a finiteness criterion for the lattice of inclusive subvarieties in the abelian-group case, giving a partial answer.
